subject: Handling post-commit surges — accounting matrix & negotiation notes
messages:
From: Olivia Price <olivia.price@vertexai.ai>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated commit: above-commit surges and billing

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the product walkthrough last week — the Dedicated capacity demo was helpful. Before we move towards a 12-month commit, the procurement team needs clarity on how Redwood handles usage that goes above the reserved commit. Specifically: 

- How do you meter above-commit usage (per-minute, per-token, per-GPU-minute)?
- Do you throttle traffic once we cross a threshold or always bill at overage rates?
- Is there any short-term grace period or surge credit for unexpected spikes?
- Can you provide an example invoice or accounting matrix so we can map to our internal chargeback?

We're trying to avoid a surprise bill if we have an unexpected training load or a large customer demo. If you could send a clear matrix + suggested contractual language for above-commit handling, that would help procurement move faster.

Olivia
Olivia Price
Head of Platform Engineering, Vertex AI Labs
olivia.price@vertexai.ai

--
Attachment: none in this note
From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference>

Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.inference>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-04-12T10:35:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated commit: above-commit surges and billing

Hi Olivia — great question and totally understandable. I've attached a simple accounting matrix and a draft amendment for your legal/procurement team. Summary below so you have the high-level terms up front: 

1) Metering model
   - Primary unit: GPU-minute (per-GPU active inference minute). We also include per-request token accounting for visibility in the console; billing ties to GPU-minute for Dedicated pools.
   - Metering cadence: 1-minute granularity with rolling 24-hour aggregation for burst detection.

2) Grace & surge handling (proposal)
   - Monthly grace band: first 10% over commit in a billing month is not charged (autofilled as a one-time smoothing credit).
   - Surge window: for bursts up to 1 hour where sustained rate <= 200% of commit, traffic will be allowed and billed at a reduced overage tier (see matrix).
   - Throttling trigger: sustained usage > 250% of commit for > 1 hour will trigger automatic soft-throttle to protect the pool; customers are notified 15 minutes before throttle.

3) Overage pricing & discounts (proposal)
   - Tier A (0-10% over): $0.00 (grace credit)
   - Tier B (10-100% over): standard overage rate (listed in matrix) with a 10% long-term customer discount if you take 12-month commit + 6 months ramp guarantee.
   - Tier C (100-200% over): higher overage unit rate with an option for a temporary surge credit (one-time per 12-month period) if the surge is due to platform migrations or demo events (requires approval).
   - Tier D (200%+): premium overage rate; may be subject to throttling policy above.

4) Contract mechanics
   - We can add a short exhibit to the SOW that codifies the grace band, threshold-based throttling, and escalation path. I attached a proposed amendment you can share with procurement.

5) Operational visibility & invoice sample
   - We will provide per-minute usage exports, a per-route cost breakdown in the Console, and a sample invoice showing how overage lines appear. See attached sample_invoice_post_commit.pdf and the overage matrix spreadsheet.

Next steps
   - If this aligns with procurement, happy to loop in Legal and generate an amendment for signature. If you'd like a deeper technical walkthrough of the metering logs, Marcus can join for a short session.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.inference

Attachments: redwood_overage_matrix_v1.xlsx, proposed_amendment_draft.docx, sample_invoice_post_commit.pdf
From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.inference>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-04-13T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: negotiation position for Vertex (RWD-4821)

Lauren / Aditya — quick note with a negotiating play to keep margin while closing the 12-month commit. Key points: 

- Ask: 12-month commit (reserved pool sizing TBD) with a 10% list discount on overage tiers if they sign within 14 days. 
- Concession: offer a 15% discounted overage rate for Tier C (100-200% over) for the first 3 billing cycles only, in exchange for a 3-month ramp guarantee (they agree to provision predictable baseline).
- Throttle fallback: keep hard throttle at 300% sustained for >2 hours (vs externally proposed 250%); that preserves us for real runaway jobs. We can advertise 250% soft-throttle with customer notif but keep stronger hard limit in contract.
- Credits: offer one surge credit (up to $5k equivalent) to cover migration/demo spikes; this is a good faith concession and limited to one use per 12-month term.

Margin impact & rationale:
- Estimated incremental margin loss for temporary concession is ~4-6% over year; closing now secures a predictable commit and Dedicated pool adoption (upsell potential on Optimize).

If you approve, I'll send an updated amendment that includes the 3-cycle discounted Tier C and the one-time surge credit language. Marcus can provide the final cost delta numbers.

Thanks,
SoOJIN
From: Olivia Price <olivia.price@vertexai.ai>

Soojin — this is very helpful, thank you. Procurement reviewed the matrix and the amendment draft and the team is broadly comfortable with the proposed structure. A couple of small asks before we sign: 

- Please include the 15% Tier C concession for months 1-3 in the amendment (we saw that in your internal note and want it codified).
- Add the one-time $5k surge credit clause with a simple approval flow (email to procurement + Redwood AM).
- Please send a DocuSign link for the amendment and a mock invoice showing the Tier B and Tier C lines populated with example numbers for our chargeback team.

If you can get that over by end of day tomorrow we can approve and route to legal.

Olivia
